The VCLT defines a [treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty "Treaty") as "an international agreement concluded between [sovereign] states in written form and governed by international law", and affirms that "every state possesses the capacity to conclude treaties." Article 1 of the VCLT restricts the application of the convention to written treaties between states, excluding treaties concluded between the states and international organizations or between international organizations.

excerpts.text: Article 26 defines *[pacta sunt servanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacta_sunt_servanda "Pacta sunt servanda")*, that agreements must be kept; Article 53 defines *jus cogens*, [peremptory norm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peremptory_norm "Peremptory norm"); Article 62 defines [Fundamental Change of Circumstance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clausula_rebus_sic_stantibus#Function_in_international_law "Clausula rebus sic stantibus"), which determines the validity or invalidity of a treaty; and Article 77 defines [depositary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depositary "Depositary"), the organisation or person who holds a multilateral treaty.
